messages:
marta: Heads up — Trivy job failing intermittently on monorepo/infra. Failing when trying to read the suppression file from the KMS-encrypted S3 object. GHAS also shows duplicate findings for the same CVE in a few repos. Can we triage?

ian: Which repo + job? any logs?

marta: repo: infra/infra-monorepo, job: scans/trivy-full. Quick log snippet:

```
2024-10-12T14:23:11Z trivy[pid=3421]: error: failed to load ignore file: s3://redwood-scanner/suppressions/infra.enc
2024-10-12T14:23:11Z aws-kms: Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt
	status code: 400, request id: 1234-abc
2024-10-12T14:23:12Z trivy[pid=3421]: scanner aborted: unable to proceed without suppression file
```

marta: Also GHAS UI shows same CVE reported twice — once as GHAS detection and once after we ingest Trivy SARIF. I think our dedupe key changed after the aggregator refactor.

devops-oncall: For the KMS error: did we recently rotate the scanner role or change the KMS key policy?

marta: We pushed a small IAM tweak to the scanner role yesterday to narrow s3 permissions. Looks like the change accidentally removed kms:Decrypt on the specific key alias.

carla: Impact on triage: which vulnerabilities are being suppressed (i.e., we depended on suppression file) vs new findings that need patching?

marta: Short list:
- CVE-2024-1177 (package: transformer-utils) — HIGH, fix available at 2.3.1, currently suppressed in suppression list
- CVE-2024-2020 (package: legacy-xml) — MEDIUM, no public exploit, suppression present
- CVE-2024-9001 (package: deps-net) — CRITICAL, not suppressed, requires immediate patch

marta: Because suppression file failed to decrypt, jobs aborting -> missing scans -> gaps in our audit logs for the last 6 hours.

tom: For GHAS duplicate findings: our ingestion pipeline tags external findings with source=trivy and GHAS native findings have source=ghas. The deduper uses (package, cve, source) right now; we should be deduping on (package, cve) only. I introduced source in the key to debug a different issue.

ian: Short-term mitigation: can we fallback to a plaintext cached suppression file in the runner image while we fix IAM?

devops-oncall: Yes — add a cached file at /opt/scanner/suppressions/current.json and change job config to prefer local file if S3/KMS decrypt fails. I'll push a hotfix to the Helm chart.

marta: Patch plan for triage:
- Emergency: deploy patch for deps-net (CRITICAL) within 24h.
- High (transformer-utils): schedule patch this week, verify tests.
- Medium and lower: keep existing suppression after we restore it; run manual review for any merging requests.

carla: Agreed. Also need to restore audit continuity. Create an incident entry for missing scan artifacts between 14:00-20:00 UTC and attach list of repos.

security-bot: Automated summary: 3 affected repos failed to produce artifacts, 12 suppressed CVEs temporarily unavailable, 1 CRITICAL unsuppressed. Incident created: INC-2024-8821.

tom: Long-term: revert the aggregator dedupe change and make dedupe deterministic by hashing (package, cve, version) and prefer highest-severity report. I'll open a PR and add integration tests.

devops-oncall: Action items I'll do now: 1) add local-suppression fallback (hotfix) 2) restore kms:Decrypt for scanner role (confirm with security) 3) rerun failed scans after ACL fix.

marta: I'll create the CVE triage ticket and assign the emergency patch to platform team.

ian: once hotfix is up, verify GHAS duplication disappears after aggregator change.

carla: +1. Also, shoutout to ops for fast rollback plan. :thumbsup:

marta: Thanks all — I'll update INC-2024-8821 with progress and close when scans are backfilled.
